subject: rstan with cores > 1 and non-standard package library location

messages.author: 5a7d96b840c23bef
messages.subject: rstan with cores > 1 and non-standard package library location
parts:
With rstan 2.7.0, stan() stops with errors with cores > 0 and R packages (Rcpp, inline and rstan in particular) in a user-specified location, It results in errors like "4 nodes produced errors; first error: there is no package called 'rstan'". This might be resolved by adding an optional argument to sampling(), say something like userLibs that a user could set to a character string vector containing the paths where they store the package libraries. Then add a statement like the following "if(!is.null(userLibs)) parallel:::clusterEvalQ(cl = cluster, .libPaths(userLibs))" before the statement "parallel::clusterEvalQ(cl, expr = require(Rcpp, quietly = TRUE))". In the mean time I guess I'll have to continue using parLapply or mclapply as before.

Thanks,
Bill

messages.author: 5a7d96b840c23bef
messages.subject: Re: rstan with cores > 1 and non-standard package library location
parts:
Yes I think so.  I am assuming you mean including a statement in sampling like:

pkgLibs <- unique(c(sub("/rstan$", "", system.file(package = "rstan")),
                                 sub("/Rcpp$", "", system.file(package = "Rcpp")),
                                 sub("/inline$", "", system.file(package = "inline")))
parallel:::clusterEvalQ(cl = cluster, .libPaths(pkgLibs))

That would probably cover the bases.

Thanks,
Bill
